title: Reverse cost-model direction: lower random_page_cost 1.5->1.0, seq_page_cost 0.8->0.6
configuration_cause: GetUserTweets consumes 87.6% of terminal capacity at p50=138us with a single Index Scan plan; the r011 upward cost-model move (random_page_cost 1.5->3.0, seq_page_cost 0.8->1.0) was refuted on TPS and inconclusive on latency, so the cost-model direction is unresolved and must be retried with a larger safe amplitude in the opposite direction.
mechanism: GetUserTweets is a single-row Index Scan (estimated_rows=1, cost 8.45) whose per-call latency dominates terminal time. With the working set fully cached (2TB RAM, shared_buffers 512MB, effective_cache_size 8GB), random reads are effectively as cheap as sequential, so the incumbent random_page_cost=1.5 over-prices index paths relative to seq_page_cost=0.8. r011 raised both costs and was refuted; the paired decision was inconclusive, not refutation of the direction. Lowering random_page_cost to 1.0 and seq_page_cost to 0.6 keeps the ratio cache-consistent and lets the planner prefer the cheapest index path for the skewed user_id predicate, reducing pages touched per GetUserTweets call and freeing terminal capacity.
query_effect: GetUserTweets remains on an Index Scan but with a cache-consistent cost model that should not penalize the index path; no plan regression expected since estimated_rows=1 already selects Index Scan.
expected_tps_effect: Small positive: freeing GetUserTweets terminal capacity by even 1-2% translates to ~300-600 rps at 32.4k baseline.
expected_latency_effect: GetUserTweets p50 and p95 decrease modestly (1-2%); other transaction types unchanged.

predictions.rationale: Cache-consistent lower random_page_cost should not change the Index Scan choice but reduces estimated cost pressure, keeping the cheapest path; p50 should not regress and may improve slightly.
Same mechanism; p95 tail should follow p50 if the index path is retained without cost-model-induced plan churn.
Freeing terminal capacity on the dominant transaction class raises completed transaction TPS.

alternatives.statement: If the cost-model change does not alter the GetUserTweets plan (already Index Scan), latency and TPS will be unchanged within noise, indicating the cost model is not the binding constraint and the bottleneck is elsewhere (e.g., WAL commit path).

If WAL commit-path queueing (wal_waiting_backends, sync_average_ms) is the true binding constraint, cost-model changes will not move GetUserTweets latency and TPS will be flat; the WAL bundle should then be revisited.

why_exceeds_incumbent: r011 tested the upward direction (random_page_cost 1.5->3.0) and was refuted on TPS; the paired decision was inconclusive, so the direction is unresolved. This proposal retries the same cost-model mechanism with a larger safe amplitude in the opposite (downward) direction, consistent with the fully-cached working set.

nodes.label: Cache-consistent cost model keeps GetUserTweets on cheapest Index Scan path

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Lower from incumbent 1.5 to safe low bound 1.0 (allowed [1.0,6.0]); reverses the refuted r011 upward direction (1.5->3.0) with a larger safe amplitude downward, consistent with fully-cached working set.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: planner cost of random/cached reads; lowering it favors index paths for the dominant GetUserTweets transaction

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Lower from incumbent 0.8 to 0.6 (allowed [0.5,2.0]); paired with random_page_cost to keep the ratio cache-consistent and reverse the refuted r011 upward move (0.8->1.0).
knob_changes.mechanism_role: I/O cost scale paired with random_page_cost; lowering it keeps the cost model consistent with cached reads
